summary.text: Julia Salazar is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for New York State Senate District 18 in Brooklyn and Queens, and she is unopposed in the general election.

A former community organizer first elected in 2018, she chairs the Senate's Crime Victims, Crime and Correction Committee and, according to her campaign website, serves as Deputy Majority Leader for Senate and Assembly Relations.

paragraphs.text: Salazar was born on December 30, 1990, in Miami, Florida.
She attended Columbia University, where, according to her official Senate biography, her advocacy began on tenant and worker issues; Wikipedia reports that she did not earn a degree there.
Before her 2018 election she worked as a community organizer with Jews for Racial & Economic Justice (JFREJ), focusing on criminal justice and police accountability.

In 2018, as a first-time candidate, she defeated incumbent Martin Malave Dilan in the Democratic primary for State Senate District 18 and won the general election, taking office on January 1, 2019; her Senate biography says she was the youngest woman elected in the history of the New York State Senate.
Salazar chairs the Senate Crime Victims, Crime and Correction Committee and previously chaired the Senate Committee on Women's Issues.
According to her campaign website, she serves as Deputy Majority Leader for Senate and Assembly Relations and as Treasurer of the legislature's Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Caucus.

Her official biography says her first bill to pass was the Comprehensive Contraception Coverage Act, that she played a key role in the 2019 Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act and that she led the 2021 HALT Solitary Confinement Act.
District 18 includes Bushwick, Cypress Hills-East New York and parts of Williamsburg in Brooklyn and parts of Ridgewood, Queens.
